title: V1 telemetry and evidence catalog, v1alpha1
description: Every signal V1 is allowed to emit, the operational or proof question each one answers, and the sensitivity and cardinality that decide where it may be placed. A field's placement is not a preference: it is derived from its sensitivity class and its cardinality class, and a placement neither class permits is a defect the suite refuses. The InferOps API emits the metrics assigned to it and writes the records specified here; every other metric is a specification for a component that is not instrumented, and each row says which it is in its emission field rather than leaving a reader to find out by scraping.

emissionStatus.meaning: The InferOps API emits the eight metrics marked emitted below and writes the structured log records this catalog specifies. Nothing else emits: the serving-runtime adapter's four metrics and the contract validator's one are specifications for components that are not instrumented, no span is produced by anything, and one metric assigned to the API has no source it is permitted to read. Every metric carries an emission field, so which is which is read from this record rather than inferred from a scrape. The only signals ever observed from another component are the serving runtime's own, in one recorded trial, listed under runtimeNativeSeries.
emissionStatus.transport: A pull endpoint and a process stream. Metrics are rendered on GET /metrics in the Prometheus text exposition format when something scrapes it, and log records are written one JSON object per line to the stream the composition point supplies. Nothing is pushed anywhere.
emissionStatus.collector: not selected; who owns a collector, store, dashboard, or alerting path is an open question in ADR 0004 and is deliberately not answered here. Nothing scrapes the endpoint and nothing collects the stream.

cardinalityBudget.rationale: A budget nobody writes down is never exceeded either, because nobody is counting. These two numbers are what the suite counts against: every metric's declared maxSeries is recomputed from its labels and refused if it disagrees or exceeds the per-metric ceiling, and the sum over active metrics is refused if it exceeds the total.
cardinalityBudget.basis: One API deployment and one serving runtime on the single-node local cluster this project targets. It is a ceiling for V1's stated environment, not a capacity claim about any store.

placements.meaning: Attached once to everything an emitting process emits, and never varied per request.
placements.retention: as long as the signal it is attached to

placements.meaning: A label on an operational metric. Every distinct combination of label values is a separate time series a store keeps for its whole retention window.

A label on an identity metric, which emits exactly one series per emitting process whatever its labels say. It is how immutable version identity is published without multiplying every other metric by it.
A named field of a structured log record.
placements.retention: the log store's retention window, which is shorter than a metric's and has to be stated before content of any kind is written to it

placements.meaning: A field in a committed evidence record under docs/proof/. Public, permanent, and not deletable in any useful sense.
placements.retention: for as long as the claim it supports stands, which is indefinite

sensitivityClasses.meaning: A value this project generates about its own operation. It describes the platform, not the caller and not the caller's data.

An identifier that reached this project through a validated workload document: a workload name, an owner, a model identifier. It is not secret and it is not free text, because the contract already constrains its form.

An identifier that attributes activity to a customer. It is not secret and it is not content, and it is still the field that turns a metrics store into a customer list and an evidence record into a disclosure.

An identifier minted per request or per span: a correlation identifier, a trace identifier, a span identifier. Its whole purpose is to be unique, which is exactly what makes it unusable as a metric label.
A prompt, a response, a chat history, or a provider error body that may quote one. This is data the project does not own and cannot classify on the caller's behalf.
Credential material, or a value read out of a place credential material is kept.

cardinalityClasses.meaning: An enumeration fixed by a specification. It grows only when a specification changes, and a reviewer sees it grow.
Bounded by how many workloads, models, or runtimes are deployed at one time. It is bounded at any instant and it is not bounded over history, which is why the budget is stated per deployment.
Bounded by the size of a published schema: a field location is one of the places the schema has. Large enough that it is a log field and never a label.
The set of values grows without limit: per request, per restart, or per release. A pod name is in this class, because a restarted pod is a new name and nothing retires the old one.
A number that is measured rather than chosen. It is the value of a signal and never the key of one.

emitters.name: The InferOps API
emitters.notes: Exists, in src/inferops/api/, and emits. It is the component that receives an inference request, so it is the only component positioned to count one, which is how ADR 0002's T7 gap is closed. Its instruments are declared in src/inferops/api/observability.py.

emitters.name: The serving-runtime adapter
emitters.notes: Exists, in src/inferops/adapters/, and emits nothing. It is the only component that sees the boundary between the platform and the runtime, so upstream failure, queue wait, and model readiness are its to report; instrumenting it is separate work and the four metrics assigned to it are marked not emitted.

emitters.name: The workload contract validator
emitters.notes: Exists as a library and a command, and emits nothing: it is invoked by a person or a test, not by a running service, so it has no process to hold a counter and no endpoint to publish one.

emitters.name: The selected serving runtime
emitters.notes: Exposes its own Prometheus text-format series on the same endpoint as its API. What it exposes was measured once, on one host; runtimeNativeSeries lists exactly that and nothing more.

signalFamilies.question: Is the platform answering requests at all, and is the model behind it ready?
What fraction of requests fail, and which named failure is responsible?
How long does a request take, and how much of that is spent waiting rather than working?
How many requests are in flight, and how many complete per unit of time?
How long does a model take to become servable, and how often does that fail?
How many tokens went in and came out, where the runtime reports them?
How much memory and processor time does the emitting process consume?
Exactly which build, model revision, and runtime image produced everything else on this page?
What did a period of operation cost, separating measured usage from estimated allocation?

correlation.assignment: The correlation identifier is assigned at the edge, by the first InferOps component to see the request, before anything downstream can fail. A refusal is then as traceable as a success, which is the case that matters: an unhandled request that never reached a handler is exactly the one nobody can find afterwards. The API does this: a well-formed X-InferOps-Correlation-ID is accepted, anything else is replaced by a generated one, and the identifier the API used is what it echoes and what every record it writes carries.
correlation.reuseAcrossRetries: A retry reuses the correlation identifier and takes a new span. The two questions are different — 'what happened to this piece of work' and 'what happened on this attempt' — and one identifier cannot answer both.
correlation.asyncRule: Across an asynchronous boundary the producer and consumer spans are linked rather than nested, and the correlation identifier is carried in the message envelope. V1 has no asynchronous boundary; the rule is stated so that the first one added does not invent its own.
correlation.placementRule: The correlation identifier, the trace identifier, and the span identifier are log fields and span attributes. None of them is ever a metric label.

headers.name: traceparent
headers.purpose: Carries the W3C trace context when a caller already has one. Absent, the edge starts a new trace rather than refusing the request. Neither this header nor tracestate is read or written by anything in this repository

headers.name: tracestate
headers.purpose: Carries vendor-specific trace state through unchanged. This project neither reads nor writes entries in it, and nothing here reads or writes the header at all

headers.name: X-InferOps-Correlation-ID
headers.purpose: Carries a business correlation identifier that survives retries and asynchronous transitions, which a span identifier deliberately does not. Read and echoed on every response, including a refusal, and validated rather than trusted: a malformed value is replaced by a generated one rather than refusing the request.

correlation.limitation: Half of this propagates and half does not, and the halves are worth telling apart. The correlation identifier and the request identifier are assigned at the edge, echoed on every response including a refusal, and written to every log record. No tracer, exporter, propagator, or SDK is selected, so no span exists: traceparent and tracestate are neither read nor written, and trace.id and span.id are specified fields that nothing populates.

attributes.name: service.name
attributes.question: Which component emitted this?
attributes.notes: Named as the OpenTelemetry semantic convention spells it, so that adopting a collector later is a configuration change rather than a rename.

attributes.name: service.version
attributes.question: Which build of that component, exactly?
attributes.notes: Unbounded over history: versions accumulate and nothing retires an old one. It is an identity attribute, so it reaches metrics only through the identity metric.

attributes.name: deployment.environment
attributes.question: Is this a development host, and may a result from it be cited as anything else?
attributes.notes: V1 has exactly one environment, `dev`. The field exists anyway, because the failure it prevents is a figure from a laptop being read as a figure from somewhere else.

attributes.name: inferops.capability.id
attributes.question: Which declared capability is this process serving?

attributes.name: inferops.release.id
attributes.question: Which release installed this, so that a regression can be tied to the change that shipped it?
attributes.notes: Releases accumulate, so this is unbounded and reaches metrics only as an identity label.

attributes.name: k8s.pod.name
attributes.question: Which replica produced this record, when one replica is behaving differently from the others?
attributes.notes: Unbounded, and the reason is worth stating: a restarted pod is a new name, so a pod label grows a metric's series count once per restart forever. It is a log field.

attributes.name: inferops.model.revision
attributes.question: Which immutable model revision produced this, given that a model identifier alone does not pin one?
attributes.notes: The distinction the contract already draws between a model identifier and the revision that pins it. A result recorded without this is not reproducible.

attributes.name: inferops.runtime.image.digest
attributes.question: Which runtime image, by digest rather than by a tag somebody can move?

attributes.name: inferops.adapter.kind
attributes.question: Which kind of serving adapter was this deployment composed with, so that a mock result stays visibly a mock result?
attributes.notes: Two values, mock and real, which is the domain's closed adapter vocabulary. It is identity rather than an operational dimension because it does not vary within a process, and because inferops.runtime.id already carries the mock runtime's registered identifier onto every operational series. It is derived from the adapter selection and never configured beside it: a second variable carrying this label would be a way to compose a real adapter and publish mock.

attributes.name: inferops.workload.id
attributes.question: Which workload is this request for, and which workload is failing?
attributes.notes: The contract constrains it to a DNS-safe name, so it is bounded in form as well as in count. The budget of 25 is a deployment ceiling, not a product limit.

attributes.name: inferops.workload.version
attributes.question: Which version of that workload document was in force?
attributes.notes: Deliberately not a metric label. Workload versions accumulate for as long as the workload exists, and a label that grows once per deployment is a label that eventually costs more than the metric is worth.

attributes.name: inferops.owner.id
attributes.question: Who is accountable for this workload when it has to be turned off?
attributes.notes: Not a metric label, because ownership is a property of the workload and joins to it. Two labels that always vary together are one label and a lookup.

attributes.name: inferops.tenant.id
attributes.question: Which tenant's activity was this, when a workload serves more than one?
attributes.notes: Excluded from metrics and from evidence records by its sensitivity class, not by anyone's discretion. A tenant label makes a metrics store a customer list, and an evidence record is public and permanent.

attributes.name: inferops.model.id
attributes.question: Which model served this, when more than one is deployed?

attributes.name: inferops.runtime.id
attributes.question: Which serving runtime answered, so that a runtime-specific failure is attributable to it?
attributes.notes: The registered runtime identifier the compatibility matrix already uses, including the mock runtime, which is how a mock result stays visibly a mock result.

attributes.name: inferops.outcome
attributes.question: Did this succeed, and if not, was the fault the caller's, ours, or a timeout?
attributes.notes: Four values: success, client-error, server-error, timeout. A timeout is separated from a server error because the two are operated differently and averaging them hides both.

attributes.name: inferops.error.code
attributes.question: Which named failure was it, in the vocabulary the caller was given?
attributes.notes: Carries a canonical code, never a message and never a provider's text. The inference error vocabulary is not published yet, so this field declares a budget rather than a value list, and the gap is recorded as a limitation.

attributes.name: inferops.rule.id
attributes.question: Which validation rule is rejecting the documents people are actually writing?
attributes.notes: Its value set is the published rule identifiers of the workload contract, which is why this is one of the few labels whose bound can be checked against something committed rather than asserted.

attributes.name: inferops.field.path
attributes.question: Where in the document was the problem?
attributes.notes: A location in the schema, never the value found there. The contract validator already refuses to repeat a value read out of a document back to the caller, and a log record is the same surface with a longer memory.

attributes.name: inferops.component
attributes.question: Which internal component failed a readiness check?

attributes.name: inferops.token.direction
attributes.question: Were these tokens read or written?
attributes.notes: Two values: input and output. One counter with a direction beats two counters whose names diverge.

attributes.name: inferops.finish.reason
attributes.question: Why did generation stop — did the caller get a whole answer or a truncated one?
attributes.notes: Deliberately carried by no metric. A rate of finish reasons answers no operational question anyone has asked yet, and a label that exists because it could exist is the way a cardinality budget is spent without a decision.

attributes.name: inferops.request.id
attributes.question: Which single synchronous request was this, as the caller was told in the response header?
attributes.notes: The identifier the API validates or mints at the edge and echoes in X-InferOps-Request-ID and in the extension member of every body. It was missing from this catalog because the catalog predates the API; a record that cannot be joined to the response a caller holds is the gap it closes. Unbounded by construction, so it is a log field and never a label - the same rule that keeps inferops.correlation.id out of metrics, for the same arithmetic.

attributes.name: inferops.correlation.id
attributes.question: Which pieces of work, across retries and components, belong to the same request?
attributes.notes: Permitted in an evidence record because a record cites a specific run and the identifier is how a reader finds it. It is not permitted as a label anywhere.

attributes.name: trace.id
attributes.question: Which trace was this span part of?

attributes.name: span.id
attributes.question: Which attempt or operation was this, within the trace?

attributes.name: inferops.duration.ms
attributes.question: How long did this particular operation take, for the one request being read about?
attributes.notes: A measurement, and measurements are values. A duration used as a metric label produces one series per distinct millisecond, which is the fastest way there is to make a metrics store unusable.

attributes.name: http.response.status_code
attributes.question: What did the caller actually receive?
attributes.notes: Bounded and safe as a label, and still not one: outcome is the dimension the metrics are cut by, and two labels that mean the same thing get used inconsistently.

attributes.name: timestamp
attributes.question: When did this happen?
attributes.notes: RFC 3339, UTC, with millisecond precision. A local-time log record is one that cannot be joined with anything.

attributes.name: level
attributes.question: How urgent is this record?
attributes.notes: Five values: debug, info, warn, error, fatal.

attributes.name: inferops.event
attributes.question: What kind of thing happened, in a form a query can match?
attributes.notes: A stable identifier such as `inference.completed` or `model.load.failed`. It exists so that a log record is queryable without matching on free-form message text, which is the field most likely to acquire a caller's data by accident.

attributes.name: inferops.retry.count
attributes.question: How many attempts did this piece of work take?
attributes.deferralReason: V1 has no retry and no fallback path. The field is registered so the first retry that is added reports itself in the agreed shape rather than inventing one.

attributes.name: inferops.cost.record.id
attributes.question: Which cost record accounts for this request?
attributes.deferralReason: The cost method that gives this field its meaning is now defined, in ADR 0007. Nothing computes, emits, or reads a cost record, so there is no value for the field to carry.

attributes.name: inferops.evaluation.decision
attributes.question: What did an evaluation gate decide about this response?
attributes.deferralReason: There is no evaluation capability in this project and none is in scope for V1. The field is registered so that a future integration adopts the name rather than coining a second one.

forbiddenFields.name: the request prompt or chat history
forbiddenFields.whyItIsTempting: It is the single most useful thing to have when reproducing a bad answer, which is exactly why it ends up in a log line during an incident and stays there afterwards.

forbiddenFields.name: the model response, whole or truncated
forbiddenFields.whyItIsTempting: A truncated response looks harmless and is not: a prefix of a customer's data is a customer's data, and truncation is not redaction.

forbiddenFields.name: an upstream error body passed through verbatim
forbiddenFields.whyItIsTempting: It is the surface most likely to be logged, pasted into a ticket, and kept, and a runtime that echoes the offending input into its error text turns a pass-through into a content capture nobody decided on.

forbiddenFields.name: the value behind a secret reference
forbiddenFields.whyItIsTempting: A debugging session wants to know whether the credential was the right one, and the fastest way to answer that is the one that publishes it.

forbiddenFields.name: an inbound Authorization or API-key header
forbiddenFields.whyItIsTempting: Whole-header logging is a one-line change and captures this without anyone choosing to.

forbiddenFields.name: a value read out of a submitted workload document
forbiddenFields.whyItIsTempting: Quoting the offending value makes an error message clearer, and it is how a secret placed in the wrong field gets copied into a log store. The field location is published instead; the value never is.

metrics.name: inferops_build_info
metrics.question: Exactly which build, model revision, and runtime image produced every other series on this endpoint?
metrics.notes: Always 1, and exactly one series per process however its labels are resolved. Its labels are identity, and putting them here rather than on every operational metric is the difference between recording immutable versions and multiplying every series by them. inferops.adapter.kind is one of them: it is how a scrape of a mock deployment is a scrape that says so.

metrics.name: inferops_inference_requests_total
metrics.question: Is the platform serving requests, what fraction of them succeed, and how many complete per unit of time?
metrics.notes: The series the selected runtime does not have. Its T7 gap is a missing cumulative request counter, and the component that receives the requests is the correct place to count them, which is what this now does. It counts requests to the inference endpoint only: a readiness probe in the same counter would make the success rate a figure about a probe loop.

metrics.name: inferops_inference_errors_total
metrics.question: Which named failure is responsible for the failures, and for which workload?
metrics.notes: Deliberately a second counter rather than an error-code label on the first. Carrying both on one counter multiplies to tens of thousands of series to answer two questions that are never asked at the same time.

metrics.name: inferops_inference_request_duration_seconds
metrics.question: How long does a request take end to end, at the tail rather than on average?
metrics.notes: Bucket boundaries are chosen for a CPU-only local runtime whose measured floor is tens of seconds, not for a hosted accelerator: eleven finite boundaries from 0.5s to 300s, and the +Inf bucket makes the twelve this row counts against. Outcome is not a label here: the budget is better spent on buckets than on separating the latency of failures, which the error counter already counts. The duration is measured on a monotonic clock, so a wall clock stepping backwards cannot produce a negative observation.

metrics.name: inferops_inference_queue_duration_seconds
metrics.question: How much of that time was spent waiting for a slot rather than generating?
metrics.emissionReason: Its emitter is the serving-runtime adapter, which is not instrumented. The API measures a request end to end and cannot decompose it: the wait for a slot happens inside the runtime, and the selected runtime reports that queueing happened rather than how long any request waited for.
metrics.notes: The one decomposition of latency that changes what an operator does: waiting means add capacity, generating means the model is the cost. The runtime's deferred-request gauge shows that queueing happens and not how long any request waited.

metrics.name: inferops_inference_requests_in_flight
metrics.question: How much work is in progress right now, and is it saturating?

metrics.name: inferops_inference_tokens_total
metrics.question: How many tokens were read and written, where the runtime reports them?
metrics.notes: Counted from the usage fields the adapter reported, and absent rather than estimated where it reported none - which is every request the committed mock serves, because the mock reports no usage. A token count derived by tokenising a prompt locally is an estimate, and an estimate certifies nothing.

metrics.name: inferops_model_load_duration_seconds
metrics.question: How long does a model take to become servable after a start, and how often does that fail?
metrics.emissionReason: Its emitter is the serving-runtime adapter, which is not instrumented. A model load is an event only the adapter sees, and the API never observes one.
metrics.notes: The measured difference between a cold and a warm start on the trial host was large enough that a single figure would have been misleading, which is why this is a histogram rather than a gauge of the last load.

metrics.name: inferops_model_ready
metrics.question: Is the model behind this workload servable right now?
metrics.emissionReason: Its emitter is the serving-runtime adapter, which is not instrumented. The API asks the adapter whether it is ready and counts the refusals in inferops_readiness_check_failures_total; the gauge that says how long a model stayed not-ready is the adapter's to hold.
metrics.notes: 1 or 0. The architecture already treats a not-ready model as a canonical refusal rather than a hang, and this is the series that says how long it was in that state.

metrics.name: inferops_readiness_check_failures_total
metrics.question: Which component is failing its readiness check, when the platform is refusing traffic?

metrics.name: inferops_workload_document_rejections_total
metrics.question: Which validation rule is rejecting the documents people are actually writing?
metrics.emissionReason: Its emitter is the contract validator, which is a library and a command invoked by a person or a test rather than a running service. It has no process to hold a counter for the life of and no endpoint to publish one from.
metrics.notes: A rule that rejects everybody is a contract defect, and it is invisible without this. The workload is not a label: attribution belongs in the log record, and a rejection is by definition a document that may not have a usable workload name in it.

metrics.name: inferops_process_resident_memory_bytes
metrics.question: How much memory is the emitting process holding?
metrics.emissionReason: Assigned to the API and not emitted by it. The only per-process memory figure the standard library exposes is /proc/self/statm, and a module under src/inferops may not read a path - the property tests/architecture/test_domain_dependency_boundary.py enforces so that the distribution stays usable from a wheel. Every other source is a runtime dependency the distribution does not declare. The exposition names this absence in a comment rather than publishing a zero, because a zero would be a measurement claiming this process holds no memory.
metrics.notes: The process's own view. Container and node resource use is a different measurement from a different source, and no such source exists here: the local cluster runs no metrics server, and the feasibility trial had to read a pod's memory from its cgroup by hand.

metrics.name: inferops_process_cpu_seconds_total
metrics.question: How much processor time is the emitting process consuming?
metrics.notes: Read from the process's own processor clock at scrape time, and set rather than incremented because that clock is already cumulative.

metrics.name: inferops_inference_time_to_first_token_seconds
metrics.question: How long does a caller wait before anything arrives?
metrics.deferralReason: V1 has no streaming path. Without one, time to first token is the same measurement as request duration, and publishing it as though it were a second signal would be a fabrication rather than a metric.

metrics.name: inferops_inference_retries_total
metrics.question: How often is work being retried or sent to a fallback?
metrics.deferralReason: There is no retry and no fallback path in V1. A counter that can only ever read zero is worse than no counter, because a flat line reads as a healthy system rather than an absent feature.

metrics.name: inferops_cost_records_total
metrics.question: How many cost records were produced for a period?
metrics.deferralReason: The cost method is now defined, in ADR 0007, and no component computes or emits a cost record. A counter that can only ever read zero would describe an absent capability as a quiet one.

runtimeNativeSeries.caveat: One scrape, on one host, on one day, from one runtime image digest. Every series below was observed in that record and none was inferred from documentation. The mapping is what the integration contract asks a capability descriptor to publish; it is not a claim that anything consumes it.

series.note: Input tokens. The direction label distinguishes it from the completion counter.
Prompt cache hits. No InferOps metric maps to it: it answers a runtime tuning question, not a platform operating one.
Prefill time. Related to latency and not the same measurement, so it is recorded rather than folded in.
A derived rate. V1 may publish no throughput figure, so it is recorded and not surfaced.
A derived rate, with the same restriction.
Instantaneous queue depth. It shows that queueing happened, never how long a request waited.
Speculative decoding, unused in the trial configuration; read zero throughout.

absentSeries.note: The runtime exposes two gauges with `requests` in the name and no counter. A gauge reading zero between requests cannot be summed, rated, or alerted on. This is the threshold ADR 0002 records as failed, and the platform closes it by counting the requests it receives itself.

logRecord.format: One JSON object per line, UTF-8, no multi-line records. A stack trace is a single escaped field, not a run of lines that a collector will split into unrelated records.
logRecord.messageRule: There is no free-form message field. A record is identified by its `inferops.event` value and carries named fields; prose that varies per request is the field into which a caller's data eventually arrives, and it is also the field no query can match on reliably.

conditionalFields.condition: when the record concerns a workload that has been identified
when the record concerns a specific version of a workload document
when the record concerns a workload that has been identified
when the workload declares a tenant and the log store's retention and access policy has been stated
when a runtime answered or refused
when the record closes a request
when the outcome is not success
when the record reports a contract validation refusal
when the record reports a contract validation refusal
when the record closes a timed operation
when the record concerns one synchronous request the API answered
when a trace context is in scope
when a trace context is in scope

events.when: the adapter has been initialized and the deployment has begun accepting work
the deployment has stopped accepting work and has begun its drain
the drain has finished and the adapter has been released
an inference request has been routed, written before anything can fail
an inference request closed with a success
an inference request closed with a canonical refusal
a readiness check answered no, naming the component that answered it

logRecord.fieldRule: A record is built through an allowlist of the attribute names published here and nothing else. There is no free-form message field, no extra mapping, and no pass-through to the encoder, so a prompt, a completion, a provider error body, a secret, an authorization header, and a value read out of a submitted document each have no name a record could carry them under. A field name outside the allowlist is refused, and the refusal names the field and never the value - the rejected field is exactly the one most likely to be carrying something that may not be repeated.
logRecord.limitation: Records are written to the stream the composition point supplies and to nowhere else. No log store, shipper, retention window, or access rule is selected, so the retention this catalog requires to be stated before content of any kind is written is still unstated. The redaction rule is now enforced by the sink rather than only by a document; what is not established is that any store keeps these records safely, because there is no store.

contentCapture.meaning: Prompts, responses, chat histories, and provider error bodies are not captured. Not sampled, not truncated, not hashed into a field that a determined reader could attack — absent.
requiresBeforeEnabling: a data classification for what would be captured, written by someone entitled to classify it
a redaction specification naming what is removed and what survives
a stated retention window shorter than the metric store's
an access control naming who may read it
a documented lawful basis and a subject-deletion path
contentCapture.note: None of the five exists. Until all five do, there is no configuration flag to turn this on, because a flag would be the whole decision. The record builder has no parameter a prompt or a response could be passed in, which is the same rule holding one layer lower down.

prohibitions.statement: No prompt, response, chat history, or value read out of a submitted document is emitted as a metric, a log field, a span attribute, or an evidence field.
prohibitions.rationale: It is data the project does not own and cannot classify on the caller's behalf, and a telemetry store is the one place from which it is never deleted.

prohibitions.statement: No credential, key, token, or value read out of a secret reference is emitted anywhere.
prohibitions.rationale: A secret in a log store is a secret that has to be rotated, and nobody finds out in time.

prohibitions.statement: No attribute whose cardinality class is unbounded or measurement is used as an operational metric label.
prohibitions.rationale: Each distinct label combination is a series the store keeps for its whole retention window, and an unbounded label is an unbounded bill and an unqueryable store.

prohibitions.statement: No correlation identifier, trace identifier, span identifier, or request identifier is a metric label of any kind.
prohibitions.rationale: Their purpose is uniqueness. A unique label is one series per request.

prohibitions.statement: A tenant identifier is a log field and a span attribute. It is not a metric label and it is not written into a committed evidence record.
prohibitions.rationale: A metrics store labelled by tenant is a customer list with a retention window, and an evidence record is public and permanent.

prohibitions.statement: An attribute marked identityOnly appears only as a label of a metric whose kind is info, and never as an operational metric label.
prohibitions.rationale: Immutable versions have to be recorded, and recording them on every metric multiplies every series by the release history. One identity series answers the question once.

prohibitions.statement: An attribute's placements are a subset of what both its sensitivity class and its cardinality class allow.
prohibitions.rationale: Placement decided case by case is placement decided by whoever is in a hurry. Deriving it from two declared classes makes an unsafe placement a failing test rather than a judgement call.

prohibitions.statement: Every attribute and every metric states the operational or proof question it answers, and no signal exists because it was available.
prohibitions.rationale: A catalogue assembled from what a library happens to expose is a cost with no reader. The question is what makes a signal removable when it stops being read.

prohibitions.statement: Each metric's declared maximum series count is recomputed from its labels and its bucket count, must agree, and must stay inside the per-metric ceiling; the sum over active metrics stays inside the total.
prohibitions.rationale: A budget nobody counts against is not a budget. Recomputing it in the suite means adding a label is a visible cost rather than an invisible one.

prohibitions.statement: Every signal family marked required is covered by at least one metric that is not deferred.
prohibitions.rationale: Availability, errors, latency, throughput, model load, tokens, and resource use are the seven questions this catalogue exists to answer. A family with no metric is a gap, and a gap is easier to see in a test than in prose.

prohibitions.statement: Every deferred attribute and metric carries a reason, and no active one carries one.
prohibitions.rationale: A deferral without a reason is indistinguishable from an oversight, and it is the form in which scope quietly reappears.

prohibitions.statement: Every native runtime series this catalogue names appears in the record that measured it, and the missing request counter is recorded as absent with the metric that covers it.
prohibitions.rationale: A mapping table is the easiest place in a repository to publish a series that does not exist, because nobody scrapes a document.

prohibitions.statement: Content capture is disabled by default and cannot be enabled by configuration. Enabling it requires five artifacts, none of which exists.
prohibitions.rationale: A capture flag with no classification, redaction, retention, access rule, or deletion path behind it is a decision made by whoever sets it during an incident.

prohibitions.statement: Every metric the API emits carries the name, instrument, label set, and bucket count this catalog declares for it, and every metric this catalog marks emitted is one the API declares.
prohibitions.rationale: A catalog that specifies one metric and a process that emits another is two records, and the one a reader trusts is the one that is wrong. Comparing them in both directions is what makes this file the source rather than a description of what somebody remembered building.

prohibitions.statement: A metric declaration whose label is not an attribute this catalog permits as a metric label is refused when the metric is declared, before any series exists.
prohibitions.rationale: The placement rules were a property of this document checked against this document. Moving the check into the registry is what turns 'a correlation identifier is never a label' from a rule a reviewer applies into an error a call site cannot get past.

prohibitions.statement: A log record is built through an allowlist of the attribute names this catalog publishes, and a field outside it is refused rather than written.
prohibitions.rationale: An exclusion list works until somebody adds the seventh field. An allowlist has no name for a prompt, a completion, a provider error body, a secret, or a value read out of a document, so there is nothing to remember at the moment it matters.

prohibitions.statement: An upstream error body is not logged verbatim and not returned to the caller. A canonical error code and the platform's own message are.
prohibitions.rationale: A runtime that quotes the offending input in its error text turns a pass-through into a content capture nobody decided on.

prohibitions.statement: Latency, throughput, and capacity series exist to operate the platform. V1 publishes no figure derived from them.
prohibitions.rationale: The project boundaries forbid publishing a performance figure in V1, and a dashboard screenshot is a publication.

evidenceTemplates.purpose: Registers what will be measured, how, and what result would count as a failure, before the run happens.
Records the host, the immutable component versions, and the digests a result depends on, so that a later run can be compared to this one.
Describes a machine-readable result set, its schema, its hash, and what was removed from it before it was committed.
Binds one public claim to the evidence for it, the certification level that evidence can support, and the limitations that travel with it.

evidenceSections.heading: Classification and certification
evidenceSections.why: The weakest label the record actually supports, and the ceiling that label carries. A record without it is read at whatever strength the reader wants.

evidenceSections.heading: Provenance
evidenceSections.why: The immutable versions: repository revision, image digests, model revision, and tool versions. A result whose inputs are named by a moving tag is not reproducible.

evidenceSections.heading: Environment
evidenceSections.why: The host, operating system, resources, and cluster the run happened on. Two of this project's accepted records are true of exactly one machine, and say so here.

evidenceSections.heading: Method
evidenceSections.why: The exact commands, in the order they were run, including the ones that failed. A method that cannot be re-executed is a description of a result rather than evidence for one.

evidenceSections.heading: Results
evidenceSections.why: What was observed, with measured values labelled as measured and derived values labelled as derived.

evidenceSections.heading: Limitations
evidenceSections.why: What the record does not establish. This is the section that stops a result being cited for something adjacent to what it measured.

evidenceSections.heading: Authorisation
evidenceSections.why: Who authorised a run that costs money, downloads a large artifact, or touches something outside the contributor's own machine, and when. 'Not required' is an answer; silence is not.

limitations.statement: The InferOps API emits eight metrics and writes seven kinds of log record. The serving-runtime adapter's four metrics, the contract validator's one, and one metric assigned to the API itself are specifications for behaviour that does not exist, and no component produces a span. Each metric's emission field says which it is.

No collector, store, dashboard, or alerting path is selected. The metrics endpoint answers when something scrapes it and nothing scrapes it; who would own a collector is an open question in ADR 0004 that this record deliberately does not answer.

No tracer, propagator, exporter, or SDK is chosen and no span exists. The correlation and request identifiers are assigned at the edge and written to every record; traceparent and tracestate are neither read nor written, and trace.id and span.id are specified fields that nothing populates.

Log records are written to the stream the composition point supplies and to nowhere else. No log store, shipper, retention window, or access rule is selected, so the retention this catalog requires to be stated before content of any kind is written is still unstated.

The serving-runtime adapter emits nothing. Queue duration, model-load duration, and model readiness are the three questions only it can answer, and instrumenting it is separate work with a separate boundary to respect.

The emitting process publishes no memory figure. The only per-process source the standard library exposes is a file, a module under src/inferops may not read one, and the distribution declares no runtime dependency that could supply another. The metric stays specified and the exposition names its absence rather than publishing a zero.

Container and node resource use has no source. The local cluster runs no metrics server, and the one recorded measurement of a pod's memory was read from its cgroup by hand. What a process sees of itself is a different measurement from what a container is charged.

The workload identity on every series and every record is deployment configuration, not a value read out of a validated WorkloadContract document. Nothing in this repository deploys a workload, so there is no document for it to come from. A workload identifier read off a caller's header would be an unbounded metric label wearing a bounded one's name, and is deliberately not read.

The selected serving runtime exposes no cumulative request counter. This was measured, it is the threshold ADR 0002 records as failed, and the platform's own counter is now emitted by the API rather than being a plan. Nothing here fixes the runtime.

The canonical error codes for inference are not published as a versioned vocabulary; the API has a closed set of eight and the contract validator has its own. The error-code label therefore carries a cardinality budget rather than a published value list, and the budget is an estimate.

The cardinality budget is arithmetic over declared bounds, not a measurement of a running system. It establishes that the catalogue is internally affordable, not that any store was tested with it - and no store has scraped this endpoint.
The four evidence templates have produced no record. They are a format, and a format is not evidence.

The latency, throughput, and capacity signals exist to operate the platform. V1 publishes no figure derived from any of them, and emitting them does not lift that restriction: a series that exists is not a figure that may be quoted.
